post.title: Why You Go Even When You Don't Want To #shorts
post.description: What did you sit through just because you paid? Tell me in the comments. Send this to the friend who finishes every bad book. Dev paid for concert tickets. He's sick, and he's still going. In 'The Psychology of Sunk Cost' (Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes, 1985), Hal Arkes and Catherine Blumer had the Ohio University theater give randomly chosen season-ticket buyers a discount. Over the first half of the season, people who had paid full price went to more plays than people who got a discount, even though the plays were the same. Money already spent can't be recovered either way, but it still pulls on our choices. It's called the sunk cost effect. Your evening costs something too. #psychology #shorts #sunkcost #overthinking #decisions
